post.summary: Ticket for an admin widget (15 minutes)
post.description: Your server asks for a ticket for the signed-in member of your staff who opens an admin widget: send their Accounts sign-in in SS-Sign-In next to the server token. The ticket is for that person and carries only the permissions of their role out of those asked for (and of switched-on features); the server token alone gets 403 needs_signed_in_staff.

permissions.description: Permissions of this product (GET /v1/permissions) the widget needs; the ticket gets those the person's role grants.

origin.description: The https origin of the page that shows the widget (a local origin while testing).

ticket.description: Give it to the admin widget (data-ticket).

get.description: The same for the admin widgets, with a ticket from POST /v1/tickets, from the origin it names.

With the browser token from the website (an Origin is required; the server token is refused): what the visitor widgets need. No feature of its own: it answers while the product serves the website and its merchant database is connected.

browserToken.description: The website's browser token: visitor routes, from https://<exact domain> or a local origin.

serverToken.description: The website's server token: the merchant's server only, never with an Origin header. On its own it runs the shop (x-ss-access: runtime): it also reaches every visitor route, acting for the visitor named by SS-Visitor-IP and, for a signed-in shopper, SS-Sign-In (their Accounts sign-in, checked for this website; a wrong, expired or foreign one is 401 invalid_sign_in). Every change of configuration and every piece of staff work (x-ss-access: staff) also needs the verified Accounts sign-in of a signed-in staff member in SS-Sign-In, whose role has the permission: a stolen server token changes nothing by itself.

ticket.description: A ticket from POST /v1/tickets: admin widgets, only from the origin it names.

SSVisitorIp.name: SS-Visitor-IP
SSVisitorIp.description: With the server token: the visitor's IP address (required on writes, else 400 visitor_ip_required). These calls count in their own window of 3,000 requests per minute per route per website, plus the per-visitor limits.

SSSignIn.name: SS-Sign-In
SSSignIn.description: The signed-in shopper's Accounts sign-in, checked for this website (a wrong, expired or foreign one is 401 invalid_sign_in). Only a verified sign-in names the shopper: a user id alone is never taken.

SSSignInStaff.name: SS-Sign-In
SSSignInStaff.description: The Accounts sign-in of the signed-in staff member whose role has the permission this call needs, checked for this website. The server token alone changes nothing: without it the call is 403 needs_signed_in_staff, with a role that lacks the permission 403 forbidden, with a sign-in of another website or an expired or forged one 401 invalid_sign_in. The person it names is who the activity log and the histories record.
